_about: bash-guard command lists. A command that names a protected path (or shares a pipeline with one
that does) may run only if its program is listed in read_only and none of its arguments matches
one of that program's exception patterns (Python regexes, searched in each argument with quotes
removed). Redirections into protected paths are always blocked.
A program given as an object also says which operands (non-option arguments) it writes:
write_operands 'all' or 'last'; those must not be protected paths. Options may come anywhere
(GNU style); value_options lists the options whose value is the next word, so it is not
counted as an operand. Every word after '--' is an operand.
Only programs seen in real use are listed. Add one when bash-guard blocks a command you need,
with exceptions for every way it can write, and a test in tests/synthetic.jsonl.

python._about: Interpreters whose name matches 'names' are allowed when bash-guard's runtime hook is installed in them (it then guards their writes and program launches while they run). 'except' patterns are checked in the interpreter's own options, before the script, -c, -m or -.

_about: Programs that run another command, described over the words shfmt splits the command into.
Prefix wrappers (timeout, xargs, ...): skip the wrapper's options (value_options take the next
word as their value unless written --opt=value), then 'positional' more words; the remaining
Embedded commands (find -exec): each run of words after a 'start' word, up to an 'end' word, is
a command; the program's own remaining words are then checked against its read_only entry.
